summary: In this GDC Festival talk, David from Wolfire Games outlines a lean, code-friendly approach to procedural animation for a human-like character in Overgrowth. He starts from a physics-first movement system driven by simple center-of-mass curves and ground-contact rules, then layers detailed animation on top with a small set of keyframes and robust interpolation. The talk covers ground rules that keep movement responsive and predictable, introduces a wheel-like technique to map ground distance to animation, and uses acceleration tilts, pose-driven keyframes, and synchronized blends to blend between walking and running. He demonstrates how to upgrade inter-frame transitions with bicubic interpolation, then introduces a spring-damper system for crouch and landing transitions. The session expands into inverse kinematics (pose matching, multi-joint IK, look targets), secondary physics for subtle bone motion, and even ragdoll concepts and “active ragdoll” ideas inspired by industry work like Euphoria. Throughout, the emphasis is on decoupling animation from core gameplay input, enabling rapid variation with fewer keyframes, and suggesting closer integration of animation with code to offload repetitive work for animators.
